seoTitle: How to Delete TradingView Chart Layouts (2026)
metaDescription: Clear out old TradingView chart layouts: open the layout menu in the chart toolbar, use the Layouts manager, and delete the setups you no longer need.
intro: Anyone who tests more than one strategy on TradingView ends up with a graveyard of saved layouts: half-finished setups, one-off experiments, copies of copies with names that meant something six months ago. They clutter the layout switcher and, on the lower plans, count against a small saved-layout limit that's stricter than most people expect. Deleting one takes seconds once you know the control lives in the chart's top toolbar, not in account settings. This guide shows where that control is, how deletion works, and what to check before removing something you can't get back.

steps.heading: Find the layout name in the chart toolbar
steps.body: Open any chart on TradingView and look along the top toolbar, to the right of the timeframe buttons and drawing tools. The name of the currently loaded layout sits there next to a small cloud icon; in a working account it might read something like "Idle For Testing" instead of anything descriptive. That name is also a button. Everything to do with saving, renaming, copying, and deleting layouts hangs off it, which is why searching your profile or account settings for a layout manager turns up nothing.

image.caption: A TradingView chart with the active layout name shown in the top toolbar, just left of the Publish button.

steps.heading: Open the layout menu, then the full Layouts manager
steps.body: Clicking the layout name drops down a menu. At the top are actions for the layout you're currently in: Save layout, an Autosave toggle, Sharing, Make a copy, Rename, and Export chart data, followed by Create new layout. Below that, under Recently used, TradingView lists the handful of layouts you've opened most recently with their symbol and timeframe. That list is a shortcut, not your full collection, so don't worry if the one you're hunting for isn't there. At the bottom of the dropdown is Open layout, and choosing it opens the Layouts dialog: TradingView's own help center calls this the "Manage layouts" list. It shows every layout attached to your account, with a search box and a sort control, and each row carries the layout's symbol, timeframe, and last-saved date.

image.caption: The layout dropdown open over the chart, with save and rename actions at the top and a Recently used list below.

steps.heading: Delete the layouts you don't need
steps.body: Hover over a row in the Layouts list and a trash icon appears on the right, alongside a star for marking favorites. Click it and confirm to remove that layout. There's no multi-select here; TradingView deletes one at a time, so a proper clear-out is a short session of repeated clicks, not one bulk action. Deletion is permanent: a removed layout doesn't go to any kind of recycle bin, and the drawings, indicator settings, and templates saved inside it go with it. If a layout has work you might want later, use Make a copy or Export chart data first, or turn on global drawing sync so your drawings survive even if the layout they were saved in gets deleted.

image.caption: The Layouts dialog listing every saved layout with its symbol, timeframe, and last-saved date, and a delete icon on the highlighted row.

steps.heading: Know your plan's actual layout limit
steps.body: Housekeeping matters more than the free Basic plan lets on: it allows exactly one saved layout, and TradingView's current pricing page puts Essential at five, Plus at ten, and Premium at ten as well. Even the top Ultimate plan caps out at ten. There's no unlimited tier for saved layouts, so if TradingView refuses to save a new one, you've hit that ceiling, not a bug, and clearing out something old is the fix. Rename what survives a clear-out while you're in there: asset class and purpose beat version numbers, so "Crypto swing" reads better in three months than "Chart 3" does.

troubleshooting.problem: TradingView refuses to save a new layout
troubleshooting.cause: You've hit your plan's saved-layout limit: one on Basic, five on Essential, ten on Plus, Premium, and Ultimate alike.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete an unused layout from the Layouts manager first, or upgrade to a plan with more room, keeping in mind that even Ultimate tops out at ten.

troubleshooting.problem: A layout got deleted by mistake and there's no way to get it back
troubleshooting.cause: TradingView removes layouts permanently with no recycle bin; the drawings and indicator settings inside go with it.
troubleshooting.fix: There's no recovery after the fact. Before deleting anything you're unsure about, use Make a copy or Export chart data on it first.

troubleshooting.problem: Drawings vanished along with a deleted layout
troubleshooting.cause: Those drawings were saved inside that specific layout instead of synced across all of them.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on global drawing sync for anything you want to keep, so it stays available on other layouts even if one gets deleted.

faq.question: Where is the delete option for a TradingView layout?
faq.answer: Click the layout name in the chart's top toolbar, choose Open layout at the bottom of the dropdown, then hover the layout you want to remove in the Layouts dialog and click the trash icon on its row.

faq.question: Can I recover a chart layout after deleting it?
faq.answer: No. Deletion is permanent and takes the drawings and indicator settings saved in that layout with it. Use Make a copy or Export chart data first if there's anything you might want back.

faq.question: How many layouts can I save on each TradingView plan?
faq.answer: One on the free Basic plan, five on Essential, and ten on Plus, Premium, and even Ultimate. There's no plan with unlimited saved layouts, so a refused save means you've hit that number, not a fault.

faq.question: Can I delete several layouts at once?
faq.answer: Not in the Layouts manager; there's no multi-select. You delete them one row at a time, which is quick but tedious for a long backlog.

faq.question: Can I delete layouts from the TradingView mobile app?
faq.answer: Yes. Layouts live on your account, not on a device, so the layout list in the mobile app shows the same collection, and removing one there removes it everywhere.

costNote: Deleting layouts is free on every plan. The reason it matters is the saved-layout cap: one on Basic, five on Essential, and ten on Plus, Premium, and Ultimate, per TradingView's current pricing page. Upgrading raises the ceiling but never removes it.
